name: 1-Testosterone (1-Test / dihydroboldenone)
lead: 1-Testosterone (1-Test, 1-T, dihydroboldenone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 5-alpha-reduced derivative of boldenone, differing from testosterone by a double bond at the 1(2) position.[1] It has been sold as a supplement or prohormone for muscle building.
According to Wikipedia, it was legally sold online in the United States until 2005, when it became a Schedule III controlled substance.[1] No clinical trials of 1-testosterone were found.

paras: A 2006 animal study cited by Wikipedia reported high androgenic and anabolic potency without prior metabolism, with strong androgen-receptor transactivation. At equimolar doses it matched testosterone propionate in growing the prostate, seminal vesicles and levator ani muscle, and unlike testosterone propionate it also increased liver weight.[1]
No studies found. The animal work above is the main published pharmacology.[1]
Doping use can be detected in urine by gas chromatography.[1]

timeline.event: Reclassified as a Schedule III drug in the United States after being sold legally online.[1]

card.summary: A DHT-derived designer steroid once sold online as a supplement; controlled in the US since 2005 and untested in human trials.
card.note: Controlled substance in the US; animal data only.

quick.overview:
1-Testosterone is a synthetic androgen sold in the past as a muscle-building prohormone.

Only animal data and doping-detection literature are described; no human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor selectively, and an animal study reported potency comparable to testosterone propionate in androgen-sensitive tissues.
quick.risks: In the animal study it also increased liver weight. It has been a US Schedule III substance since 2005.
